p: 3,898 people estimated sleeping rough (autumn 2024, latest published)
s: MHCLG statutory rough-sleeping snapshot: 3,898 people sleeping rough on a single night in autumn 2024, up 20% on 2023
d: Rough sleeping in England rose to 3,898 in autumn 2024, a 20% increase year-on-year and the highest since records began. In 2026 the government published a landmark £2bn Rough Sleeping Strategy (manifesto commitment to end rough sleeping), creating 2,400 long-term supported homes and funding prevention services. CICs can bid via the Ending Homelessness in Communities Fund.
src: MHCLG rough-sleeping snapshot 2024; GOV.UK Rough Sleeping Strategy 2026

s: NHS England RTT: 7.6 million people waiting for treatment (latest published 2025)
d: The NHS waiting list stands at 7.6 million; 3.1 million have waited over 18 weeks. Under the 2025/26 NHS 10-Year Health Plan, neighbourhood health services and same-day community care are being prioritised, with VCSE partners expected to take a larger prevention role.
src: NHS England RTT 2025; NHS 10-Year Health Plan 2025

s: DWP / Households Below Average Income: 4.3 million children (29%) in relative poverty after housing costs, 2023/24 (latest published)
d: Child poverty rose to 4.3 million (29%) in 2023/24. The government's Child Poverty Strategy was published in December 2025 (updated July 2026) with prevention-focused measures; the two-child limit and benefit cap remain in place as of 2026, so statutory levers for immediate income lift are limited and CIC prevention work fills the gap.

s: Scottish Government: 24% of children in relative poverty 2023/24
d: Scotland's child poverty rate is 24%, with a statutory target to cut it to 10% by 2030/31 under the Child Poverty (Scotland) Act. Glasgow has the lowest life expectancy in the UK.

s: Welsh Government: 28% of children in relative poverty
d: Wales has the highest working-age poverty rate in Britain; 28% of children in poverty. The Welsh Government's Child Poverty Strategy centres on income maximisation and VCSE delivery.

p: 1 in 4 adults with a mental-health condition
s: NHS Digital: 1 in 4 adults experience a mental-health condition; NHS talking-therapy waiting lists exceed 1 million
d: Demand for NHS mental-health services is at record high; 1.4 million people are waiting for talking therapies. The 2025 Mental Health Bill and the NHS 10-Year Plan shift toward community-based, neighbourhood mental-health support, an opening for CIC/VCSE delivery.

s: London Councils: over 183,000 Londoners in temporary accommodation, a record high
d: London has a record 183,000 people in temporary accommodation; Newham and other East London boroughs have the highest concentrations. Driven by benefit caps and private-rent unaffordability. The 2026 Rough Sleeping Strategy's prevention services are directly relevant here.
src: London Councils TA stats 2025; GOV.UK Rough Sleeping Strategy 2026

s: Greater Manchester combined authority: 132,410 households in TA, highest outside London
d: Greater Manchester has 132,410 households in temporary accommodation — the highest outside London. With the Prime Minister's office now based in Manchester ('No 10 North'), regional mayors hold key housing/policy roles, creating a direct route for CIC commissioning.

s: Birmingham City Council: family homelessness and TA placements at multi-year high
d: Birmingham's household homelessness and temporary-accommodation use are at a multi-year high after the council's section 114 notice and housing-market pressure. Eligible for the Ending Homelessness in Communities Fund.
src: Birmingham City Council 2024; GOV.UK Communities Fund 2026

s: Campaign to End Loneliness: ~3.5 million people in England chronically lonely
d: An estimated 3.5 million people in England are chronically lonely, with the highest rates among young adults, the bereaved and those with long-term conditions. The NHS 10-Year Plan names social prescribing and VCSE connectors as core prevention.
src: Campaign to End Loneliness 2024; NHS 10-Year Plan 2025

p: Food bank use at record high
s: Trussell Trust: 3.1 million emergency food parcels distributed in 2023/24
d: Trussell Trust distributed 3.1 million emergency food parcels in 2023/24, a record, with universal-credit claimants the largest user group. With the two-child limit and benefit cap still in place in 2026, income-based prevention remains constrained.
